distinguish between them by noting that effusions appear radiopaque (white) while pneumothorax appears radiolucent (black).", "If the mediastinum is shifted ipsilaterally (towards the opacity), diagnose volume loss causes such as lung collapse, atelectasis, or fibrosis.", "Rule out consolidation (pneumonia) as a primary cause for significant mediastinal shift, as it typically preserves lung volume or causes only minimal shift unless associated with substantial collapse."]}, {"category": "reasoning", "trigger": "When evaluating a frontal chest X-ray showing left superior mediastinal widening and mild cardiomegaly in a patient with unexplained hypoxaemia or dyspnoea.", "steps": ["Identify the specific location of mediastinal widening: confirm it is localized to the left superior mediastinum (often appearing as a vertical density parallel to the aortic knob) rather than a diffuse mass or right-sided deviation.", "Assess the lung fields for signs of pulmonary congestion or edema; note if they are clear despite the presence of cardiac silhouette enlargement.", "Correlate the anatomical finding (widened left superior mediastinum) with the physiological symptom (hypoxaemia) by considering a Persistent Left Superior Vena Cava (PLSVC) draining into the left atrium.", "Distinguish this from left heart failure (which would typically show pulmonary venous congestion) or compressive masses (which would not inherently cause shunting/hypoxaemia without airway compromise)."]}, {"category": "relationship", "trigger": "When evaluating a chest X-ray or CT for suspected congenital lung anomalies, specifically looking for the 'scimitar sign' and associated vascular findings.", "steps": ["Inspect the right hemithorax on the chest X-ray for a curvilinear opacity running parallel to the right heart border (the scimitar vein).", "Assess the position of the mediastinum and trachea; determine if there is deviation toward the side of the anomalous vein (rightward shift) and check for ipsilateral lung hypoplasia.", "On cross-sectional imaging (CT), trace the course of the anomalous vein to confirm drainage into the inferior vena cava and identify any systemic arterial supply originating from the abdominal aorta to the lower lung lobe."]}]
